reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports that Cu-rich grain boundaries reduce strength and ductility and promote grain boundary sliding/dislocation slipping under uniaxial tension. However, it does not address high-temperature sliding wear, the effect of reducing Cu segregation, or the translation of tensile deformation mechanisms to wear resistance, leaving several key premises unsupported.
premises: Cu-rich grain boundaries lower strength and ductility in FeNiCrCoCu HEA under tension
Cu segregation causes uneven stress distribution and promotes grain boundary sliding and dislocation slipping
Reducing Cu segregation will improve grain boundary cohesion
Improved grain boundary cohesion will reduce wear and deformation during high-temperature sliding
Molecular dynamics tensile results translate to high-temperature sliding wear mechanisms
